scores.evidence: In Moffatt v. Air Canada (2024), a tribunal held the airline liable for its chatbot's made-up refund policy
scores.rationale: Claims about RAG mechanics, pgvector suitability, legal precedent, EU AI Act Art. 50, and webhook reliability limits are all accurate, with real limits stated rather than overstated.

scores.evidence: A chat widget on the help center that answers customer questions using only published help-center articles, cites them, and hands off
scores.rationale: Solves exactly the stated problem, resolves ambiguities (public docs, no account access, one language) with explicit assumptions, and defers out-of-scope items with reasons.

scores.evidence: The CMS stays the source of truth for content (the bot never writes to it), and the help desk stays the source of truth for tickets
scores.rationale: Clear data ownership, consistent choices honored across phases (grounded-only policy enforced in prompt, claim-check, renderer, and gates), and no internal contradictions.

scores.evidence: An LLM judge checks each claim and is calibrated against 150 human-graded answers
scores.rationale: Gates V0–V6 target the specific risks (faithfulness, leakage, injection, cost), thresholds are labeled ASSUMPTION, risky checks precede customer exposure, and validation continues in production via daily sampling and a holdout canary.

scores.evidence: If any of them is wrong, the phase order changes, so please check them first
scores.rationale: Four load-bearing assumptions stated up front with explicit consequences if false, and all numbers tagged ASSUMPTION/UNKNOWN/BASELINE with named owners to confirm them.

scores.evidence: The bot states a policy or makes a promise... that the docs don't support, customers act on it, and the company is held to it
scores.rationale: Identifies the hardest domain failures (ungrounded promises, withdrawn-policy staleness, injection via planted article content, runaway spend, provider outage) each with concrete detection, containment and recovery; only ticket-creation idempotency on retry is unaddressed.

scores.evidence: 1 chat service, 1 ingest worker, pgvector inside the Postgres you already run; owning team's existing on-call
scores.rationale: Deploy/rollback via flag, image and index-alias swap, domain-meaningful signals (freshness lag, faithfulness, spend), named ownership and runbooks, all sized to a small team.

scores.evidence: Cost per resolved conversation: UNKNOWN, set against the cost of a human-handled ticket, which support ops must supply
scores.rationale: The dominant driver (inference) is capped per turn/session/day with a kill-switch, cost gates the rollout, build-vs-buy and self-host trade-offs are explicit, and unknown figures are flagged rather than invented.

scores.evidence: R3: a non-public article shown to the public can't be unshown
scores.rationale: Decisions carry explicit reversibility ratings, revisit triggers and exit paths; the costly-to-reverse ones (privacy boundary, indexing scope, answer policy) get the most scrutiny while reversible defaults are decided quickly.

scores.evidence: Monolith instead of services... No agent framework, plain code... a reranker only if V4 needs it
scores.rationale: The simplest workable design (one service, pgvector in existing Postgres, fine-tuning and routing deferred) with complexity added only where the liability-heavy domain demands it.

scores.evidence: Run the V4/V5 question set against a trial of the vendor agent
scores.rationale: The Phase 0 slice is concrete enough to start today, ordering is justified by dependency and risk, every phase has checkable exit criteria, and every gate specifies what changes if it fails.

checklist.evidence: Index updates from CMS webhooks plus a nightly full reconcile. Unpublish events take a priority path
Heading-aware chunking... Index versioned with embedding model and chunker
≥ 300 real questions from search logs and ticket subjects, sampled by top contact reasons, with the expected article labeled by support staff
Answer only from retrieved passages, with citations. Decline and offer handoff when retrieval is weak or a claim isn't supported
For refunds, billing, pricing, legal and security, give a link to the article plus a handoff... Agents rate handoffs as usable
user and retrieved text, which go in as clearly marked data, never as instructions... no ticket created without a user click
Index only articles the CMS marks public and published. Filter when indexing, and check visibility again when answering
Personal data is removed before logs and analytics. Raw transcripts stay in our region with 30-day retention... no retention and no training
The bot only answers questions and hands off to a human. It doesn't look up accounts or take actions like refunds
Daily automated faithfulness check on 2% of chats, plus a weekly human review... Send content gaps to the docs team
Per turn: ≤ 12k input and ≤ 1k output tokens... Daily spend kill-switch... Cost per resolved conversation... set against the cost of a human-handled ticket

traps.evidence: Decline and offer handoff when retrieval is weak or a claim isn't supported
Filter when indexing, and check visibility again when answering... retrieval checks the caller's permissions (new costly-to-reverse decision)
Prompt + RAG instead of fine-tuning (fine-tuning is deferred)... CMS webhooks, nightly reconcile, priority unpublish path
Evals run in CI on every prompt or model change
No agent framework, plain code... with a reranker only if V4 needs it

note: An exemplary plan: all eleven checklist items concretely addressed, all five traps explicitly recognized and avoided, with risk-ordered gates, labeled assumptions, and a proportionate architecture; the only nameable gaps (handoff idempotency, no dollar estimate) are deliberate or trivial.
